title: Ὁδοιπόροι καὶ πλάτανος
titleEn: The Travellers and the Plane Tree
part: The Travellers and the Plane Tree (Chambry 257)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 257. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὁδοιπόροι θέρους ὥρᾳ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ὑπὸ καύματος τρυχόμενοι, ὡς ἐθεάσαντο πλάτανον, ὑπὸ ταύτην καταντήσαντες καὶ ἐν τῇ σκιᾷ κατακλιθέντες ἀνεπαύοντο.
sentences.tr: Hodoiporoi therous hōrāi peri mesēmbrian hypo kaumatos trychomenoi, hōs etheasanto platanon, hypo tautēn katantēsantes kai en tēi skiāi kataklithentes anepauonto.
sentences.l: Travellers, in the season of summer around midday, being worn down by the burning heat, when they caught sight of a plane tree, having come under it and having lain down in the shade, were resting.
sentences.i: Travellers in the summer season, about midday, worn out by the heat, caught sight of a plane tree, came under it, lay down in its shade and rested.
sentences.n: θέρους ὥρᾳ is a dative of time, 'at the season of summer'. καῦμα is the burning heat of noon rather than warmth in general, and τρυχόμενοι, a present passive participle, has them being worn away by it as they walk.

sentences.t: Ἀναβλέψαντες δὲ εἰς τὴν πλάτανον ἔλεγον πρὸς ἀλλήλους ὡς ἀνωφελές ἐστιν ἀνθρώποις τοῦτο ἄκαρπον τὸ δένδρον.
sentences.tr: Anablepsantes de eis tēn platanon elegon pros allēlous hōs anōpheles estin anthrōpois touto akarpon to dendron.
sentences.l: But having looked up at the plane tree, they were saying to one another that this fruitless tree is useless to men.
sentences.n: ὡς after a verb of saying introduces the report, and the Greek keeps the tense the speakers themselves used — ἐστιν, 'is', where English shifts to 'was'. Note also that πλάτανος is feminine: the tree answers in the next line as 'she'.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ ὑποτυχοῦσα ἔφη· « Ὦ ἀχάριστοι, ἔτι τῆς ἐξ ἐμοῦ εὐεργεσίας ἀπολαύοντες, ἀχρείαν με καὶ ἄκαρπον ἀποκαλεῖτε. »
sentences.tr: Hē de hypotychousa ephē· « Ō acharistoi, eti tēs ex emou euergesias apolauontes, achreian me kai akarpon apokaleite. »
sentences.l: But she, taking-up-the-word, said: « O ungrateful ones, while still enjoying the benefit that comes from me, you call me useless and fruitless. »
sentences.n: ὑποτυχοῦσα is the house idiom for breaking in with a reply, not for any physical seizing; it is feminine because πλάτανος is. ἀπολαύω takes the genitive of what one enjoys, and τῆς ἐξ ἐμοῦ εὐεργεσίας packs the prepositional phrase inside the article — 'the benefit-from-me'.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τινὲς ἀτυχεῖς εἰσιν ὡς καὶ εὐεργετοῦντες τοὺς πέλας ἐπὶ τῇ χρηστότητι ἀπιστεῖσθαι.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn tines atycheis eisin hōs kai euergetountes tous pelas epi tēi chrēstotēti apisteisthai.
sentences.l: So too, among men, some are so unlucky as, even while doing good to those near them, to be disbelieved in the matter of their kindness.
sentences.i: So too, among men, some are so ill-fated that even when they do good to their neighbours they are distrusted for their very goodness.
sentences.n: ὡς with the infinitive ἀπιστεῖσθαι makes a result clause, 'so as to be disbelieved'. ἐπὶ τῇ χρηστότητι gives the ground on which the distrust falls: it is their very goodness that is not believed in.
